rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: An Easie and plaine Method Teaching How to judge upon NATIVITIES
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: A separate natal-astrology treatise begins, distinct from the completed Book II horary questions.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Original PDF521 is a title page with no printed Arabic page number.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The title announces a procedure for rectifying a natal birth time.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Not itself a supplied executable birth-time correction rule.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Trutine of Hermes Animodar or by Accidents
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The title lists Trutine of Hermes, Animodar and significant life accidents as alternative rectification approaches.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Different methods with potentially different inputs and assumptions.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The treatise promises judgments using the twelve astrological houses.
rows.original_source_qualifications: House meanings are historical beliefs not human behavioral validity.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly announces directions, revolutions, profections and transits.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Separate timing mechanisms not actually described on the title page.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: exact Measure of Time in Directions
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He also advertises methods for computing the timing of directions.
rows.original_source_qualifications: A book promise, not verified predictive performance.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: London printed by Tho Brudenell for Partridge and Blunden 1647
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The book includes its 1647 London printers and publishers.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Bibliographic first-edition witness; next natal pages must be interpreted under this provenance.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: verso of Book III title page
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The reverse side of the nativity title is essentially blank apart from print-through.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Source-order metadata only; no astrological calculation or prediction extracted.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Table converting Hours and Minutes of time into Degrees and Minutes of the Aequator
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The new natality introduction begins with a tabular conversion of clock time into equatorial angular displacement.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Numerical/astronomical conversion, not event prediction.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: One hour of time corresponds to fifteen degrees of the equator.
rows.original_source_qualifications: 360 degrees divided by 24 hours.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The twenty-four-hour row corresponds to a complete 360-degree rotation.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Full-turn modulo 360 applies in subsequent computation.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: one minute time fifteen minutes equator
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: One minute of clock time corresponds to fifteen arcminutes of equatorial angle.
rows.original_source_qualifications: 0.25 angular degrees per minute of time.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Four minutes of civil time correspond to one angular degree.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Reciprocal form used later as minutes divided by four.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: columns hour degree minute time minute angle
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The printed reference has separate hour-to-degree and minute-to-degree columns with row values.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Complete table numerals require independent transcription; only structure and load-bearing examples checked.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Sixty time minutes correspond to fifteen degrees.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Source last minute row is visibly printed as sixty to fifteen degrees.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The source begins an instruction subsection on converting time into equatorial right ascension.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Book III introduction, not yet the numbered rectification chapter.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: erecting a Figure by Tables Regiomontanus
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says the conversion is used when erecting a chart by the tables of Regiomontanus.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historical house-construction algorithm.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: one hour makes fifteen degrees in Aequator
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He reiterates 15 angular degrees for one hour of time.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Numerical rule repeated from printed table.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: one minute hour makes fifteen minutes of Aequator
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He states fifteen arcminutes per minute of clock time.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Scale factor, not new independent observation.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: convert hours before and after noon
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Hours around noon are converted to angular degrees/minutes before chart construction.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Original time convention requires calendar/local hour input.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He calls the resulting angular measure the right ascension of time.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Distinguish RA of elapsed time from right ascension of the Sun.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He adds right ascension of time to the Sun's right ascension.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Requires original solar ecliptic longitude and a right ascension table.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He maps resulting equatorial angular amount via right ascensions to an ecliptic degree for the tenth-house cusp.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Ascendant still needs a separate oblique ascension step.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The worked chart time is printed Saturday 12 June 1647 at 3:25 PM.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historical local civil time and Old Style date not independently resolved.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly gives the Sun at 0°51 of Cancer.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Sun longitude is source-provided, not independently recomputed.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He rounds the Sun's Cancer longitude to one whole degree.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Introduces a source-authorized approximation before table lookup.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: At 1° Cancer the printed right-ascensions table yields 91°05′ for the Sun.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This numerical value is original example context and needs direct independent table validation.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Three elapsed hours convert to 45 angular degrees.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Exact multiplication by 15.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Twenty-five time minutes convert to 6°15′.
Right ascension Sun 91°05′ plus time conversion 51°15′ yields 142°20′.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Arithmetic independently checkable, but input solar longitude is historical.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly reads the corresponding ecliptic position as approximately 20° Leo for the tenth-house cusp.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historical table lookup, chart system and rounding parity open.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: add ninety degrees to Mid-heaven RA
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly instructs adding 90° to right ascension of the tenth-house cusp before Ascendant lookup.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This is the formal step of his Regiomontanus house-construction procedure.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The first-edition print appears to claim adding 90° to 142°20′ produces 230°20′.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Numerically false: 142°20′ + 90° = 232°20′, a two-degree discrepancy. Do not silently repair either printed value.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Independent integer-arcminute arithmetic gives 232°20′.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Contradicts the printed 230°20′, retained as explicit historical numerical error.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Table of Oblique ascensions belonging to 53 latitude
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He routes the result into the oblique-ascension table corresponding to geographic latitude 53°.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Latitude-specific data rather than universal sign mapping.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: degree of the ascendant for that Elevation
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The description of using the 53° oblique table to find the Ascendant continues onto PDF525.
rows.original_source_qualifications: One continuous calculation, not separate horoscopes.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says 230°20′ is not listed exactly in the oblique-ascension table.
rows.original_source_qualifications: He follows the printed 230°20′ rather than mathematically implied 232°20′.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He says 5° Scorpio corresponds to oblique ascension 230°52′ at 53° latitude.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Look-up of a specific printed source-table cell; machine-independent parity incomplete.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He says to interpolate a proportional fraction to obtain a less than five-degree position.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Interpolation interval and rounding should be verified before encoding a fully reliable calculator.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Ascendant four degrees and more not fully five
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He concludes the Ascendant is about four degrees of Scorpio, not fully five.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Numerical result depends on the internally inconsistent 230°20′ premise.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: more exact nativity than ordinary questions
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He distinguishes precise nativity figure computation from less meticulous ordinary horary questions.
rows.original_source_qualifications: A method preference, not empirical evidence natal charts are accurate.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly indicates the following four tabular groupings support erecting a figure.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Count refers to groups/types, whereas the full physical source runs over many page faces.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The examples are pedagogical approximations for beginning students.
rows.original_source_qualifications: An introduction rather than a fully worked independent rectification outcome.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly offers direct arithmetic conversion of clock hours into equatorial degrees without consulting the first table.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Equivalent to the linear 15° per time hour relation.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He instructs dividing minutes of time by four to obtain degrees of equatorial arc.
He reiterates adding the time angle to the Sun's right ascension for the midheaven.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Depends on chosen reference time and precise Sun RA.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if more than three hundred sixty cast away 360
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He reduces angular totals over 360° by subtracting a full turn.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Modular arithmetic for zodiacal/RA angles.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He maps the resulting right ascension to the corresponding ecliptic position using the right-ascensions table.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Data-dependent conversion, not pure linear arithmetic.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly recommends punctual chart erection for nativities.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This is original pedagogical precision advice, not observed predictive improvement.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The book supplies a numeric table mapping zodiac sign/degree to right ascension degrees/minutes.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Physical page PDF526; original table cells preserved in image, not independently fully re-keyed.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Aries Taurus Gemini Cancer Leo Virgo
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The first leaf contains six columns for the first six signs.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Per-sign degree rows 0–30 with Gr. M. columns.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: At 0° Aries the table starts at 0° right ascension.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This is a load-bearing verifiable equinoctial anchor, not proof all cells verified.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Cancer first degree 91 degrees five minutes
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The 1° Cancer row gives right ascension about 91°05′, matching the prose example on PDF524.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Direct source table reference with minute precision, no independent contemporary ephemeris parity.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: residue of Table of Right Ascensions

rows.original_source_qualifications: PDF527 follows PDF526 with no gap.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Libra Scorpio Sagittarius Capricorn Aquarius Pisces
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The remaining six sign columns fill the 180–360° equatorial sequence.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The first degree row for Libra begins at 180° right ascension.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The final Pisces sign boundary wraps to 360°/0°.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: A six-sign-per-leaf oblique ascension lookup begins.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Different from right ascension, and dependent on geographic latitude.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Original PDF529 explicitly labels this pair as for latitude 34°.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: sign degrees right/left first and last six

rows.original_source_qualifications: Rows are not independently all keyed; original source preserves every cell.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly uses oblique ascension, rather than generic right ascension, to determine local ascendant.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Another six-sign-per-leaf table supplies oblique ascension.
